batch_strategy: Paired condition-response and loading contrasts, tail coverage, and interval-pathology repair

feedback_interpretation: Previous measured outcomes strengthened the case for scaffold-specific condition curves, loading contrasts, and separate V2 repair. The feedback showed both large late-elution underprediction and substantial V2 overprediction under extreme loading, so a single monotonic solvent or global loading correction is inadequate. Several measured rows also exposed invalid or implausibly narrow predicted intervals, supporting direct interval-pathology checks. The batch therefore emphasizes paired local curves and chemically varied tail labels while retaining targeted calibration repair.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local curves for m159, m173, and m177; tail-response anchors across polar, multifunctional, aromatic carbonyl, sulfur-containing, and fused aromatic families; four direct interval-pathology experiments; and several high-cw or less represented scaffolds. Repeated conditions teach solvent and loading interactions, while distinct tail chemistries improve transfer beyond the already sampled molecules. This covers common interpolation regions, rare high-V1/V2 rows, loading extremes, and V2-dominant failures that can materially improve overall Row-distribution generalization.
